A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LayerNorm Scaling research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Their equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original pre-training, fine-tuning, layer-pruning, representation and vision experiments, including results in Tables 1–8 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a layerwise Jacobian analysis of a pretrained LLaMA2-7B model in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same inverse-square-root layer-index scaling in Equation (12). The vision-specific placement variants also already appear in v2. The new Jacobian analysis does not alter the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The language-modeling, downstream-task, C4 representation, ImageNet-1K and MMMU coverage is retained. The new LLaMA2-7B diagnostic adds a model configuration within existing coverage, without a documented new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including DeepNorm, Mix-LN, scaled initialization, LayerScale, SkipInit, Admin, Group-LN and Sandwich-LN. Figure 5 examines layers of one pretrained model and introduces no comparator against LNS.

E3.justification: Figure 5 adds a diagnostic protocol measuring token-averaged Jacobians at five layers of pretrained LLaMA2-7B. The previously reported training budgets, learning rates, model configurations and benchmark evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.1 adds a Jacobian case study probing identity-like behavior with increasing depth. Existing pruning, angular-distance, variance and scaling-placement analyses, including those in the appendices, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Token averaging in the new heatmaps is aggregation for that diagnostic, not added uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds qualitative Jacobian results described as increasing diagonal dominance and diminishing off-diagonal entries. Existing numerical results are unchanged; for example, Table 1 retains LNS perplexities of 25.76 for LLaMA-130M and 15.71 for LLaMA-1B.

T1.justification: The assumptions, lemmas, theorems, equations and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Apparent equation differences arise from spacing and extraction order. The new heatmaps provide an empirical illustration without revising the formal argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about Pre-LN causing ineffective deep layers, LNS mitigating this problem, and benefits for pre-training and fine-tuning. Figure 5 is offered as additional support for an existing claim.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets the new Jacobian heatmaps as empirical evidence of collapse toward identity mappings. v2 asserted identity-like behavior through its theoretical discussion but lacked this specific interpretation of measured Jacobians. The applicability qualifications and Appendix D limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The added diagnostic identifies LLaMA2-7B, layers 3, 6, 9, 24 and 31, and token averaging, providing limited reproducibility information. Its input data, token count and Jacobian computation details are unspecified. Existing implementation details and code access are unchanged; the initialization warning is relocated.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. The scaled-initialization citations accompanying the abstract footnote already accompanied the same warning in v2's introduction.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short explanation in Section 3.1 and moves the scaled-initialization warning from the introduction to the abstract. The overall section organization and nearly all prose are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the five-panel Jacobian heatmap as Figure 5. Existing Figures 5–9 become Figures 6–10, and several retained tables and figures shift position as the text reflows. Their substantive displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figure 5 makes the proposed mechanism more inspectable, and relocating the initialization warning improves its visibility. However, diagonal dominance alone does not establish closeness to identity, and the relationship between the plotted LayerNorm Jacobians and the full Transformer-block Jacobian in Equation (5) is insufficiently explained. With the method, proofs and benchmark evidence unchanged, the diagnostic benefit and interpretive ambiguity leave the net quality effect uncertain.
